# Classroom Labs

> Classroom Labs is the home of a family of free, interactive learning sites for science, math, coding and reading, made by one independent maker. Every lab is free to use with no sign-up. They are made for classrooms: they work on Chromebooks and can be shared as a link in Google Classroom, Canvas or Schoology. The science, math and reading labs have printable activities with teacher answer keys. A paid teacher plan for teachers and schools is being planned; teachers can join its waitlist on this site.

## Science

- [Interactive Periodic Table](https://interactiveperiodictable.net/) (Chemistry, Middle and high school): Explore all 118 elements, compare their properties, combine elements into real compounds and balance chemical equations. Main tools: [Periodic table](https://interactiveperiodictable.net/), [3D atom viewer](https://interactiveperiodictable.net/atom-viewer), [Chemistry sandbox](https://interactiveperiodictable.net/sandbox), [Equation balancer](https://interactiveperiodictable.net/equation-balancer), [Identifying ions practical](https://interactiveperiodictable.net/identifying-ions), [Periodic table quiz](https://interactiveperiodictable.net/quiz). [For teachers](https://interactiveperiodictable.net/teachers): Printable worksheets for the sandbox, balancing equations and identifying ions, each with an answer key, plus lesson ideas for the other tools.
- [Physics Lab](https://thephysicslab.org/) (Physics, Grades 7–12): Run simulations of motion, forces, energy, waves, circuits and light: launch a projectile, swing a pendulum, build a circuit and bend a ray of light. Main tools: [All physics experiments](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/), [Projectile motion](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/projectile-motion/), [Pendulum](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/pendulum/), [Ohm’s law circuit](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/ohms-law/), [Practice problems](https://thephysicslab.org/practice/). [For teachers](https://thephysicslab.org/teachers/): A printable activity and answer key for every experiment, NGSS connections and a worksheet builder.
- [Biology Lab](https://thebiologylab.org/) (Biology, Grades 6–12): Cross parents in a Punnett square, translate DNA into protein, take apart a 3D cell and model how a population grows. Main tools: [Punnett square calculator](https://thebiologylab.org/punnett-square-calculator/), [DNA to protein](https://thebiologylab.org/dna-transcription-translation/), [3D cell model](https://thebiologylab.org/cells/3d/), [Label the cell](https://thebiologylab.org/cells/label-the-cell/), [All biology tools](https://thebiologylab.org/tools/). [For teachers](https://thebiologylab.org/teachers/): Twelve printable classroom activities with answer keys and NGSS connections.
- [Earth Science Lab](https://earthsciencelab.org/) (Earth science, Grades 5–10): Locate an earthquake from seismograms, move tectonic plates, read a contour map, carve a river and follow water and rock through Earth’s cycles. Main tools: [Earthquake epicenter finder](https://earthsciencelab.org/tools/earthquake-epicenter/), [Plate tectonics explorer](https://earthsciencelab.org/tools/plate-tectonics/), [Contour map playground](https://earthsciencelab.org/tools/contour-map/), [Rock cycle builder](https://earthsciencelab.org/tools/rock-cycle/), [All earth science labs](https://earthsciencelab.org/tools/). [For teachers](https://earthsciencelab.org/teachers/): A one-page activity and answer key for each lab, how to run them in 10 to 15 minutes, and NGSS connections.
- [Astronomy Lab](https://theastronomylab.com/) (Space, Grades 6–12): Set a planet’s orbit, step through the Moon’s phases and the seasons, line up an eclipse and find an exoplanet in a star’s light curve. Main tools: [Orbit simulator](https://theastronomylab.com/labs/orbit-simulator/), [Moon phases](https://theastronomylab.com/labs/moon-phases/), [Seasons simulator](https://theastronomylab.com/labs/seasons/), [Eclipse simulator](https://theastronomylab.com/labs/eclipses/), [All astronomy labs](https://theastronomylab.com/labs/). [For teachers](https://theastronomylab.com/teachers/): Printable worksheets with answer keys and NGSS connections for the simulations.

## Math

- [Geometry Lab](https://geometrylab.net/) (Math, Grades 6–12): Solve a triangle with worked steps, read the unit circle, transform shapes on a grid and print nets to fold into 3D shapes. Main tools: [Triangle solver](https://geometrylab.net/triangle-solver/), [Unit circle](https://geometrylab.net/unit-circle/), [Transformations](https://geometrylab.net/tools/transformations/), [Printable nets](https://geometrylab.net/printable-nets/), [All geometry tools](https://geometrylab.net/tools/). [For teachers](https://geometrylab.net/teachers/): Printable student activities with answer keys and Common Core connections.

## Coding

- [KidsCode](https://kidscode.dev/) (Coding): Guide a robot, snap code blocks together and write first real Python programs.

## Reading

- [Fiction & Fact Library](https://fictionandfactlibrary.com/) (Reading, Grades 2–8): Build a plot diagram, sort facts from opinions, tag the parts of speech and follow Aesop’s fables read aloud. Main tools: [Plot diagram builder](https://fictionandfactlibrary.com/tools/plot-diagram/), [Fact or opinion](https://fictionandfactlibrary.com/tools/fact-or-opinion/), [Parts of speech](https://fictionandfactlibrary.com/tools/parts-of-speech/), [Fables read-along](https://fictionandfactlibrary.com/tools/fables/), [All reading tools](https://fictionandfactlibrary.com/tools/). [For teachers](https://fictionandfactlibrary.com/teachers/): One-page worksheets, teacher answer keys and short lesson plans for every tool.

## This site

- [Classroom Labs: Free Interactive Labs for Every Classroom](https://classroomlabs.org/): Free interactive labs for science, math, coding and reading. No sign-up, made for classrooms, and they work on Chromebooks and in Google Classroom.
- [About Classroom Labs: Free Learning Sites for Class](https://classroomlabs.org/about/): Classroom Labs is the home of eight free, interactive learning sites for science, math, coding and reading, made by one independent maker for classrooms.
- [Contact Classroom Labs](https://classroomlabs.org/contact/): How to contact Classroom Labs: questions about the free labs, corrections, ideas for the teacher plan, and requests to delete a waitlist signup.
- [Privacy Policy](https://classroomlabs.org/privacy/): How Classroom Labs handles data: no accounts, no student data, what the teacher plan waitlist stores and why, Cloudflare as processor, 12-month deletion.
- [For Teachers: Free Labs, Activities and Answer Keys](https://classroomlabs.org/teachers/): How teachers use the free Classroom Labs in class: share a link in Google Classroom, Canvas or Schoology, print activities with answer keys, no logins.
